summary.plain: Combining 280 days of running, LZ again saw no dark matter and set the tightest limits yet on how weakly a heavy dark matter particle could interact with ordinary matter.
summary.technical: WS2024: 4.2 ± 0.1 tonne-years (280 live days) with new 214Pb beta tagging and a newly identified 124Xe double-capture recombination background. No excess; leading spin-independent and spin-dependent limits above 9 GeV/c2, reaching 2.2e-48 cm2 at 40 GeV/c2 (median sensitivity 5.1e-48 cm2).

title: Dark Matter Search Results from 4.2 Tonne-Years of Exposure of the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) Experiment
why_it_matters: With 4.2 tonne-years of data, about twenty times the first run, LZ set the world's strongest limits on heavy WIMP dark matter and demonstrated new background-tagging techniques that the field will need as detectors approach the irreducible neutrino background.
